jurisdiction.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has no AI-specific law and no published AI strategy. AI appears in the 2019 Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, which includes an action to launch AI projects, and in the 2023 Code du numérique, which gives the National Digital Council a remit over AI ethics and sets rules on automated decisions and impact assessments; the Code's official text could not be read because the official gazette was unavailable. In August 2026 the post and telecoms regulator (ARPTC) began asking providers of AI platforms to file a declaration describing their models, data, hosting and policies on bias, human oversight and transparency. A first national AI strategy was validated by the government in August 2026 but has not been published, and a national data governance strategy with a data and AI skills pillar is online but undated.
lead_institutions: Autorité de Régulation de la Poste et des Télécommunications du Congo (ARPTC)
narrative.review_notes: In October 2026 the Presidency, the Prime Minister's office, the Ministry of Digital Economy, the Senate and the post and telecoms regulator were searched again, and the regulator's AI platform declaration form was added; the official gazette, the National Assembly and the central bank sites could not be accessed. The 2023 Digital Code, the national AI strategy, the data governance strategy and the 2026 ministerial orders on digital services remain leads, and the standards and procurement bodies are still to be checked.

instruments.english_title: National Digital Plan "Horizon 2025" (For a connected and high-performing DRC)
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Republic (Office of the Head of State; Special Adviser to the Head of State in charge of Digital), drafted by the Cadre de Concertation of digital-sector experts
instruments.current_status: Validated at the national validation workshop on 5 September 2019 (opened by the President on 3 September 2019) and published by the Presidency (document dated September 2019). Its 2025 horizon has passed; a successor Plan National du Numérique 2026-2030 (PNN2) and a first national AI strategy (SNIA) were being prepared by the Ministry of Digital Economy in 2025-2026 but no official text was found online as of 12 October 2026 (see leads), so this plan is not recorded as superseded.
instruments.summary: The DRC's national digital plan to 2025, built on four strategic pillars (infrastructure; content; applications/uses; governance and regulation) broken down into strategic axes, objectives, actions and a chronogram of priority actions. It is a digital strategy rather than an AI strategy, but its infrastructure pillar includes an action to initiate projects in artificial intelligence, augmented reality, robotics and related fields and to create research centres, and it sets out an institutional framework for implementing the plan.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The country's only published national digital strategy with explicit AI actions; precursor to the national AI strategy under preparation.

instruments.official_title: Formulaire de déclaration de fourniture des plateformes d’intelligence artificielle
instruments.english_title: Declaration form for the provision of artificial intelligence platforms
instruments.issuing_authority: Autorité de Régulation de la Poste et des Télécommunications du Congo (ARPTC)
instruments.current_status: Published as an online declaration form on the regulator's website on 7 August 2026. The form requires the declarant to commit to the Digital Code; the page does not state which implementing text makes the declaration compulsory for AI platform providers.
instruments.summary: The telecoms and digital regulator's official form for providers of artificial intelligence platforms in the DRC to declare their services (new declaration, renewal or modification). Declarants must describe the AI services offered (including text, image, audio and video generation and autonomous agents), the sectors served, the models used and where they are hosted, the data processed and whether the model keeps learning from user data, and say whether they have policies on responsible use, bias, human oversight, errors, hallucinations and illicit content, along with security measures and certifications such as ISO/IEC 42001. They must also sign a sworn statement committing to the Digital Code and to its rules on personal data protection, cybersecurity and transparency in the use of AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific regulatory requirement found for the DRC: a regulator-run declaration procedure for AI platform providers that collects information on transparency, data, human oversight and risk-management practices.

leads.title: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code du numérique
leads.english_title: Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Digital Code
leads.issuing_authority: President of the Republic (ordinance-law; ratified by Parliament)
leads.note: Main AI-relevant binding law: art. 12 tasks the Conseil National du Numérique with overseeing the ethics of advanced digital tech, including AI; Book II Title III (personal data) creates an Autorité de protection des données, gives a right to information on automated decision-making including profiling, and art. 245 requires a data protection impact assessment for systematic automated evaluation/profiling producing legal effects. Text (168 pp., 'Fait à Kinshasa, le 13 mars 2023', in force on promulgation) was read only from a non-official copy (discovery). No official full text could be reached: the Journal officiel (journalofficiel.cd) returned HTTP 503 to curl and WebFetch, ARPTC (arptc.gouv.cd) and leganet.cd failed (TLS/503), and the Secrétariat Général au Numérique site (numerique.gouv.cd) is a placeholder. Record as binding_law / binding-law, data-privacy, government-governance, ethics once the official JO text is reachable. Update 2026-10-18: the Official Journal site was still in maintenance (service unavailable); the regulator (arptc.gouv.cd) and Ministry of Digital Economy (economienumerique.gouv.cd) sites opened but neither hosts the Code's full text. ARPTC's official 'Activités et services numériques' page confirms the Code sets declaration, authorisation and homologation regimes for digital services. Still held as a lead.

leads.title: Stratégie Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle (SNIA) de la République Démocratique du Congo
leads.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the DRC
leads.note: Drafting launched 8 October 2025 with PNN2; technical validation workshop 23-24 July 2026; presented and validated by members of the Government on 4 August 2026 and to be submitted to the Council of Ministers for formal adoption (press reports only). No official text or Council of Ministers record found online on 12 October 2026 (primature.gouv.cd and presidence.cd searched). Record as national_strategy once published; it may supersede the PNN Horizon 2025 for AI. Update 2026-10-18: no text on the Ministry of Digital Economy's documents page, Primature search or Presidency; ARPTC's official 'Activités et services numériques' page lists a 'Plan Stratégique de l'Intelligence Artificielle' among national strategies but gives no text or date. Still unpublished.

leads.title: Stratégie Nationale de Gouvernance des Données (SNGD) de la RDC
leads.english_title: National Data Governance Strategy of the DRC
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Economy (prepared with UNECA support)
leads.note: Found 2026-10-18 on the Ministry of Digital Economy's official documents page (economienumerique.gouv.cd/mediatheque/documents; PDF hosted on the ministry's file host, 85 pp.) and read. Data governance strategy with six strategic orientations; includes a strategic priority to build a national pool of data and AI skills (AI training, support to the African Centre for AI Research CARIA, data/AI modules at ENA). The foreword is unsigned and undated ('Fait à Kinshasa, le ...'), so no publication or adoption date can be stated. AI is a skills pillar inside a data strategy: held as a lead; record as strategy if an adopted, dated version is published.
